To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the showerhead cooling performance on turbine blade leading edge is influenced by mainstream Reynolds number, blowing ratio and the radial angle.
the showerhead radial angle has a significant effect on the cooling performance and the pressure loss.
showerhead film cooling is a good choice for the leading edge region and the radial angle of showerhead hole has a marked influence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the film cooling performance of the leading edge region on a turbine blade with the use of IR thermography.
the showerhead film cooling performance at leading edge of turbine blade, which is important for the design and optimization of turbine blade cooling.
the film cooling effectiveness of showerhead film cooling geometry at the leading edge of a turbine blade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
45° shower head radial angle is the best leading edge film cooling configuration for this test blade.
the 45° shower head radial angle gives the best cooling performance in terms of cooling effectiveness, heat transfer coefficient, and aerodynamic loss.
the cooling effectiveness is strongly dependent on the blowing ratio and the mainstream Reynolds number.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the showerhead film cooling with 90° radial angle is the most effective in terms of the cooling effectiveness and pressure loss, and the showerhead cooling on pressure side has a better performance than that on suction side.
the showerhead radial-angle cooling holes with 45° are more effective for the leading edge cooling than the streamwise-angle cooling hole.
45° radial angle is the best choice for the showerhead film cooling at leading edge region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
showerhead film cooling is a very effective way to protect the blade from hot gases and can be used to reduce the blade cooling air consumption.

the IR thermography technique is an efficient and effective tool to investigate film cooling performance on turbine blades, and the leading edge film cooling performance is strongly dependent on the showerhead hole angle.
showerhead film cooling with 45° radial angle can provide a good balance between cooling performance and pressure loss.
